title: The De Bruijn–Erdős Theorem on Incidence Geometry and Near-Pencil Tightness
abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the De Bruijn–Erdős theorem (1948) in incidence geometry and pairwise balanced block designs, together with its constructive near-pencil tightness proof. Proves that any finite linear space on n ≥ 3 non-collinear points determines at least n lines (|P| ≤ |L|) via the classical combinatorial double-counting inequality. Furthermore, explicitly constructs the near-pencil configuration with designated apex p₀ (consisting of one line of n - 1 points and n - 1 lines of 2 points) and proves that it forms a valid linear space achieving exact equality |L| = |P|. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).
